new_statements.quote: The WIZ word consists of one stressed (or primarily stressed) syllable. (A polymorphemic word may also have 1 or 2 secondarily stressed syllables, as described in section 5.3) ... 5.1 Stress in WIZ is contrastive, as seen in the following examples: 'du1la3 <sin> du1'la2 <large shawl> 'be12ga2 <gourd> be2'ga3 <necklace> However, in most cases, stress is predicatable, as it usually occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word. (In polymorphemic words stress occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word stem.) When stress does not occur on the penultimate syllable, it occurs on the final syllable. ... There are a few words which function on the phrase level and have no stress.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Each word has one primary stress. Default position is the penultimate syllable of the (monomorphemic) word, and in inflected/polymorphemic words the penult of the stem (aspect prefix + root), with bound person markers and enclitics following as post-stressed syllables (up to 4-5 of them). A lexical minority of words have final stress instead, so stress position is contrastive within a final two-syllable window of the stem (minimal pairs dula 'sin' vs dulá 'shawl', bega 'gourd' vs begá 'necklace'; 2016 grammar adds beku/bekú, sina/siná, inda/indá etc.). Long and glottalized ('broken') vowels occur only in stressed syllables. Tone (H, M, L + 4 contours) is a separate lexical system on every syllable. The 2016 Gramática (sec. 2.3, p. 16) restates the same rule in Spanish: 'la gran mayoria de las palabras zapotecas tienen acento en la penúltima sílaba... Se escribe el acento solamente cuando el acento cae en la última sílaba.'
new_statements.secondary_stress: Sec. 5.3 (ms p. 50): 'Secondarily stressed syllables occur only in polymorphemic words. All bound person markers except <3rd person common> and <1st person plural, inclusive> receive secondary stress'; bound demonstratives -ni3 'here' / -na2 'there' and augment markers -do12 / -do3 also carry secondary stress; secondarily stressed vowels are checked by lenis glottal closure utterance-finally. 3rd-common -ni3/-na2 and plural clitic ka2- are unstressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Lexically final-stressed words (e.g. be2'-dia12 'eagle', be2'la?21 'ravine', zhu2'ban3 'tail'; contrastive pairs above); a few phrase-level function words (ki2ni1 'because', na2 'and') have no stress; at most one prestressed syllable per monomorphemic word, apparent two-prestress words (za2ge2'o12 'coyote') analysed as old compounds; one CVV+CV item ku1'u2ku2 'dove' (marked 'loan') stresses the second vowel; Spanish loans treated in sec. 6 (not examined).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word stem, not the full inflected word: person-marker suffixes and enclitics (-ni3, -na2, ka2-, -a1 'not here') are post-stressed, so in verbs like 'ru2xa3ka2na2 'they are carrying' primary stress sits three or more syllables from the word end. Forms cited are isolation/citation forms with raised-numeral tone marking (1 high, 2 mid, 3 low).
new_statements.identity_note: Both Thiessen sources explicitly describe the Santa Ana Yareni dialect of 'Western Ixtlán Zapotec' (WIZ), i.e. exactly yare1249 / ISO zae. Thiessen 1989 notes neighbouring towns (Teococuilco de Marcos Pérez, San Miguel/San Isidro Aloápam) speak slightly different dialects; Aloápam Zapotec has its own code (zaq, aloa1234) and is not covered.
